examples.knowledge_point: Defining a Set Conditionally Using the Roots of a Polynomial
examples.problem:
Find the missing coefficients $p$ and $q$ in the conditional definition of the set given below.

$$
\{\pm 3\textrm{i}\} = \Big\{z \in \mathbb{C} \: : \: 4z^2+pz+q = 0 \Big\}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
The given set contains the roots $z\in\mathbb C$ of some quadratic polynomial $f(z).$

Since the quadratic polynomial has roots $z_1=-3\textrm{i}$ and $z_2=3\textrm{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=4,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(z) & =a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) \\  & =4\cdot (z-(-3\text{i}))(z-(3\text{i})) \\  & =4\cdot (z+3\text{i})(z-3\text{i}) \\  & =4\cdot ({z}^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}) \\  & =4\cdot ({z}^{2}-9{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & =4\cdot ({z}^{2}+9) \\  & =4{z}^{2}+36\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express the given set as follows:

$$
\{\pm 3\textrm{i}\} = \Big\{z \in \mathbb{C} \: : \: 4z^2+\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0}z+\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}36} = 0 \Big\}
$$

Finally, $p=0$ and $q=36.$

feedback.problem:
Describe the set $S={5,6,7,…}$ using a conditional definition.

$$
N
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The set $S$ contains all natural numbers greater than or equal to $5.$

Therefore, the set can be written as

$$
S={x\in N\,:\,x\ge 5}.
$$

**Note**: This definition is not unique. For example:

- We can write $x\in Z.$ This gives

$$
S={x\in Z\,:x\ge 5}.
$$

- We can write $x>4.$ This gives

$$
S={x\in N\,:\,x>4},
$$

or, writing $x\in Z$ as before, we have

$$
S={x\in Z\,:\,x>4}.
$$
